what_this_is: candidate labs for a lab-in-the-loop partnership, built ONLY from the public professional record: published papers, lab pages, public talks. No contact details, no personal inferences.
the_rule_on_quotes: every quote is verbatim and sourced, or it is not here. A paraphrase is marked as one. A fabricated quote attributed to a real person would be the worst thing this project could produce.

candidates.name: Jacob M. Daane
candidates.institution: University of Houston, Department of Biology and Biochemistry
candidates.field: Comparative and functional genomics of fish form; evolution of relative size and proportion in paired fins; phylogenomics of teleost skeletal traits.
candidates.why_relevant_to_delphi: He is the closest match in the field to the exact quantity our fin-ratio programme is built on. The pectoral-fin allometry in development/allometry.json is a log-log fit WE computed over 49 specimen rows from his 2021 Data S1A (b = 1.058 +/- 0.020 SE, r2 = 0.983), and the two loci his paper puts at the centre of fin proportion — lat4a and kcnh2a — are two of the three genes our winged-zebrafish design edits. Our genotype thread independently settled lat4a = slc43a2a against his annotation. He is therefore the one person who can say whether our re-fit of his data is a legitimate use of it, and whether the design we built on top of it asks a question he has not already answered. Separately, his record of intersecting a phylogenomic signal with a mutant screen is the closest existing instance of the loop we are trying to close.

flagship_papers.title: Modulation of bioelectric cues in the evolution of flying fishes
flagship_papers.why_it_matters: Supplies both the specimen measurements our fin-ratio fit is computed from and the two loci our design edits, in one paper.

flagship_papers.title: Historical contingency shapes adaptive radiation in Antarctic fishes
flagship_papers.why_it_matters: Shows the method we would be buying into: a genome-scale comparative signal tested by making the predicted change in zebrafish.

flagship_papers.title: Genetic Screen for Postembryonic Development in the Zebrafish: Dominant Mutations Affecting Adult Form
flagship_papers.why_it_matters: 72 adult-viable mutants of adult shape — the empirical answer to "which body proportions are even reachable by single mutations", which our design layer assumes rather than knows.

flagship_papers.title: The origin and evolution of dorsal determination mechanisms in vertebrate paired appendages
flagship_papers.why_it_matters: A current, 13-author, multi-country fin-patterning paper — evidence the relevant work is live and already runs as a consortium.

key_figures_or_findings: Phylogenomic analysis across 35 species of flying fishes and relatives recovered coding and regulatory signatures of convergently enlarged paired fins (Curr Biol 2021, doi 10.1016/j.cub.2021.08.054, via PubMed).
lat4a (an L-type amino acid transporter) and kcnh2a (a potassium channel) regulate fin proportion in zebrafish, and their interaction phenocopies flying-fish fin proportions (same paper).

Antarctic notothenioid study: targeted sequencing of >250,000 loci across 46 species; altered trip11, col1a2 and col1a1a function in zebrafish phenocopies the skeletal reduction (Nat Ecol Evol 2019, doi 10.1038/s41559-019-0914-2, via PubMed).
Adult dominant screen: 72 adult-viable mutants, linked mutations identified for 22 of 25 mutants analysed (Genetics 2017, doi 10.1534/genetics.117.300187, via PubMed).

real_quotes.quote: Changes to allometry, or the relative proportions of organs and tissues within organisms, is a common means for adaptive character change in evolution. However, little is understood about how relative size is specified during development and shaped during evolution.
real_quotes.source_title: Modulation of bioelectric cues in the evolution of flying fishes
real_quotes.context: Opening sentences of the published abstract (PubMed record for PMID 34534441). This is the gap statement our fin-ratio programme is aimed at, in his words rather than ours.

real_quotes.quote: We show that interaction between these genetic loci in zebrafish closely phenocopies the observed fin proportions of flying fishes.
real_quotes.source_title: Modulation of bioelectric cues in the evolution of flying fishes
real_quotes.context: From the same abstract. The existence of this result is also the main reason a naive version of our proposal is already done.

public_record: Runs the Daane Lab at the University of Houston; the lab page carries the tagline "Evolutionary and developmental genetics @ University of Houston" (https://www.daanelab.org/).
The lab page posted "New funding from NSF!" on 1 Aug 2024 (no amount or award number is given on the page, and none is asserted here).
Senior/corresponding author on the 2019 Nature Ecology & Evolution notothenioid paper and first author on the 2021 Current Biology flying-fish paper.
candidates.collaboration_angle: The natural ask is small and concrete: a read on whether our re-fit of his published specimen measurements is sound, and whether the fin-proportion prediction our model makes is distinguishable from what his lat4a x kcnh2a double already shows. If it is, the bench arm is one he is already equipped for. WE would have to bring: the full derivation of the allometric fit with its residuals and the alternative linear fit, the explicit statement of which of our numbers are measured versus assumed (the .organism file does this mechanically), and the negative results below stated up front — in particular that our guide ranking is uninformative, which means WE cannot promise him a good guide and should not pretend otherwise.

openness_evidence.claim: Publishes the per-specimen measurements behind the fin allometry as supplementary data (Data S1A), which is how we were able to re-fit it at all.
Works in large multi-institution teams: the 2026 Current Biology paper has 13 authors across the US, Spain and Slovakia.
Comfortable moving between comparative genomics and a zebrafish bench test in the same study, which is structurally what a lab-in-the-loop partnership is.
openness_evidence.source: Our reading of the design of doi 10.1038/s41559-019-0914-2 and doi 10.1016/j.cub.2021.08.054. He has not said he wants external computational partners.

candidates.caution: He may have the least to gain of anyone on this list, because he has already done the experiment our design is pointed at. The honest framing is that we are asking for correction of our use of his data, not offering him a discovery. There is also a real chance the first answer is "your fit is fine and the prediction is already published", which would end the collaboration at one email and should be accepted gracefully. Finally, a new-ish lab is the worst place to spend four months of tank space on someone else's untested prediction.

candidates.name: Matthew P. Harris
candidates.institution: Boston Children's Hospital (Orthopaedic Research Laboratories) and Harvard Medical School, Department of Genetics
candidates.field: Genetics of adult/postembryonic skeletal form in fishes; size, shape and proportion regulation; forward genetics on adult phenotypes; fin-to-limb comparative development.
candidates.why_relevant_to_delphi: Our whole fin-size programme sits inside the literature his lab built. kcnk5b — the gene our top-ranked bench case overexpresses, with the W169L allele our structures thread modelled — comes from his 2014 paper, and the key uncomfortable fact in our bench brief is from that lineage too: in this programme loss of function does not change fin size, so only precise gain-of-function changes are informative. That single constraint is what turned our plan from a knockout into an overexpression experiment. His 2021 Cell paper is also the sharpest existing counter-example to our morphology scorer: zebrafish carrying supernumerary long bones in the pectoral fin are animals whose trait vector our scorer has never seen and would have no basis to rank.

flagship_papers.title: Bioelectric signaling regulates size in zebrafish fins
flagship_papers.why_it_matters: The source of kcnk5b, of the gain-of-function logic our bench case inherits, and of the somatic-transgenesis design our proposal copies.

flagship_papers.title: Latent developmental potential to form limb-like skeletal structures in zebrafish
flagship_papers.why_it_matters: Demonstrates reachable fin anatomies that are outside any trait distribution we have fitted — i.e. the exact region where our plausibility scorer is blind.

flagship_papers.title: Zebrafish eda and edar mutants reveal conserved and ancestral roles of ectodysplasin signaling in vertebrates
flagship_papers.why_it_matters: Establishes dose-sensitive, organ-specific responses and buffering of adult skeletal phenotypes — a direct warning that a single predicted ratio may not be robust to genetic background.

flagship_papers.title: Modulation of bioelectric cues in the evolution of flying fishes
flagship_papers.why_it_matters: Senior author on the paper our fin-ratio fit is computed from.

key_figures_or_findings: alf mutants carry gain-of-function mutations in kcnk5b, a two-pore-domain potassium channel; the mutations raise K+ conductance and hyperpolarise the cell, and the channel must be able to conduct K+ to enlarge fins and barbels (PLoS Genet 2014, doi 10.1371/journal.pgen.1004080, via PubMed).

kcnk5b acts locally within the mesenchyme of fins and barbels — which is why our bench case scores overgrowth against marker-positive mesenchyme in the same fin rather than against injection status (same paper).

Activating mutations in vav2 and waslb produce supernumerary long bones in the pectoral fin that integrate into musculature and form joints; the phenotype requires Hox11 function (Cell 2021, doi 10.1016/j.cell.2021.01.003, via PubMed).

eda/edar loss affects fin rays, scales and pharyngeal teeth but not early development, with substantial buffering across genetic backgrounds (PLoS Genet 2008, doi 10.1371/journal.pgen.1000206, via PubMed).

real_quotes.quote: The scaling relationship between the size of an appendage or organ and that of the body as a whole is tightly regulated during animal development.
real_quotes.source_title: Bioelectric signaling regulates size in zebrafish fins
real_quotes.context: First sentence of the published abstract (PubMed record for PMID 24453984). It is the premise our fin-ratio traits assume without testing.

real_quotes.quote: Our findings reveal a latent, limb-like pattern ability in fins that is activated by simple genetic perturbation.
real_quotes.source_title: Latent developmental potential to form limb-like skeletal structures in zebrafish
real_quotes.context: Closing sentence of the published abstract (PubMed record for PMID 33545089). We cite it as the clearest published evidence that reachable fin morphologies extend outside the cloud our scorer was fitted to.

public_record: Runs the Harris Laboratory ("Fishbone Lab") in the Orthopaedic Research Laboratories at Boston Children's Hospital, part of the Genetics Department at Harvard Medical School (https://research.childrenshospital.org/research-units/fishbone-lab).
The lab page states it uses forward genetics in fishes to find variants regulating adult form, and runs comparative genomic and embryological studies in other fish species.
Corresponding author on the 2014 PLoS Genetics, 2021 Cell, 2021 Current Biology and 2026 Current Biology papers above.
candidates.collaboration_angle: Two distinct asks, and they should not be mixed. (1) A sanity read on our top-ranked bench package before anyone orders anything — it is built directly on his 2014 design, including the DsRed-only and non-conductive GFG->AAA controls, and the missing piece we already know about is a positive control for transposition in the host facility. (2) The more interesting one: his vav2/waslb fish are a ready-made adversarial test set for our morphology scorer. If we can score his published supernumerary-bone animals and the scorer calls them typical, that is a result for us and costs him nothing but permission and a measurement protocol. WE would have to bring: the full package with its stop rules and traps list, the per-animal return format, and an explicit statement that the guide ranking we would otherwise hand him is worthless on zebrafish.

openness_evidence.claim: Released a community resource of 63 stable Gal4 enhancer-trap transgenic lines explicitly framed as "a useful resource for the zebrafish community".
The lab page states its position allows productive interaction with clinical researchers at the hospital; it names no external computational collaborators.

Routinely co-authors across institutions and countries (Tubingen, Washington University, Toronto, Lehigh, Wheaton, Santander, Seville, Bratislava across the papers above), so an external partner is structurally normal for this lab.
openness_evidence.source: Our reading of the author affiliation lists on the four flagship papers, retrieved from PubMed. He has not stated an interest in external computational partners.

candidates.caution: He is the originator of the biology we are proposing to re-test, which cuts both ways: high relevance, but also the highest chance that our prediction is either already known to him or already known to be wrong. A clinically embedded lab has no obvious use for a computational plausibility score, and our strongest current offer to him is a list of our own failures. The 2014 construct is also not in a public repository, so one branch of our own plan is effectively a request for a reagent from the Tubingen authors, which is a favour, not a collaboration — asking for both at once would be too much.

candidates.name: Miguel A. Moreno-Mateos
candidates.institution: Andalusian Centre for Developmental Biology (CABD), Pablo de Olavide University / CSIC / Junta de Andalucia, Seville, and Department of Molecular Biology and Biochemical Engineering, Pablo de Olavide University
candidates.field: In vivo CRISPR-Cas methodology in fish embryos: guide-activity determinants and prediction, alternative nucleases and PAM-relaxed variants, RNA targeting, homology-directed repair.
candidates.why_relevant_to_delphi: Our CRISPR guide-ranking benchmark is literally built on his data. The 499 sgRNAs with measured mutagenesis in injected zebrafish embryos are from the CRISPRscan paper he first -authored; we located 307 of them uniquely in GRCz11 and scored three models against the measured activity. The result is that the score our design pipeline ranks guides by (Doench 2014 Rule Set 1) comes out at rho = -0.037, CI [-0.149, 0.073], and our own heuristic at 0.082, CI [-0.024, 0.196] — both straddling zero — while his CRISPRscan reaches 0.269, CI [0.165, 0.364]. We state openly that 0.269 is an upper bound rather than an estimate, because it is being scored on the study that fitted it. The obvious next piece of work is an INDEPENDENT zebrafish activity set, and he is the person most likely to know whether one exists or could be generated cheaply.

flagship_papers.title: CRISPRscan: designing highly efficient sgRNAs for CRISPR-Cas9 targeting in vivo
flagship_papers.why_it_matters: Both the ground truth and the only model that beat chance in our benchmark; its Supplementary Table 3 is the coefficient set we reimplemented and verified.

flagship_papers.title: CRISPR-Cpf1 mediates efficient homology-directed repair and temperature-controlled genome editing
flagship_papers.why_it_matters: Shows editing efficiency in fish is temperature-dependent — a covariate our guide-ranking benchmark does not model at all.

flagship_papers.title: CRISPR-Cas13d Induces Efficient mRNA Knockdown in Animal Embryos
flagship_papers.why_it_matters: A knockdown route that sidesteps the gain-of-function constraint blocking several of our fin cases.

flagship_papers.title: Genome editing in animals with minimal PAM CRISPR-Cas9 enzymes
flagship_papers.why_it_matters: Tests 40 sites in two species and reports how far the CRISPRscan algorithm transfers to new nucleases — the generalisation question our benchmark is about.

key_figures_or_findings: Guanine enrichment and adenine depletion increase sgRNA stability and activity in vivo, while differential sgRNA loading, nucleosome positioning and Cas9 off-target binding were not major determinants (Nat Methods 2015, doi 10.1038/nmeth.3543, via PubMed).

CRISPRscan: a predictive sgRNA-scoring algorithm fitted on sgRNAs with activity measured in injected zebrafish embryos (same paper). In OUR benchmark its Spearman rho on 307 of those guides is 0.269, CI [0.165, 0.364] — reported by us as an upper bound because the scoring set is its own training set.
CRISPR-RfxCas13d gave a 76% average decrease in transcript levels in zebrafish embryos and worked in medaka, killifish and mouse embryos (Dev Cell 2020, doi 10.1016/j.devcel.2020.07.013, via PubMed).

SpG and SpRY mutate in vivo at a lower rate than SpCas9 at equivalent formulations, recoverable by optimising mRNA-gRNA or RNP concentration, across 40 targets in zebrafish and C. elegans (Nat Commun 2022, doi 10.1038/s41467-022-30228-4, via PubMed).

real_quotes.quote: However, variable activity across different single guide RNAs (sgRNAs) remains a significant limitation.
real_quotes.source_title: CRISPRscan: designing highly efficient sgRNAs for CRISPR-Cas9 targeting in vivo
real_quotes.context: Second sentence of the published abstract (PubMed record for PMID 26322839). It is the problem our benchmark says our own pipeline has not solved.

real_quotes.quote: We also found that the CRISPRscan algorithm could help to predict SpG and SpRY targets with high activity in vivo.
real_quotes.source_title: Genome editing in animals with minimal PAM CRISPR-Cas9 enzymes
real_quotes.context: From the published abstract (PubMed record for PMID 35552388). This is a published transfer test of his own model, which is why he is the right person to ask about an independent held-out activity set.

public_record: Principal investigator at the CABD, a joint CSIC / Pablo de Olavide University / Junta de Andalucia centre in Seville; listed in the Pablo de Olavide research portal under the CABD and the Department of Molecular Biology and Biochemical Engineering (https://investiga.upo.es/investigadores/160221/detalle?lang=en).
CRISPRscan is distributed as a public web tool (https://www.crisprscan.org/), which is how the model reached our pipeline in the first place.
Corresponding author on the 2017 Nature Communications, 2020 Developmental Cell and 2022 Nature Communications papers above.
candidates.collaboration_angle: Not an animal-time ask at all, which makes it the cheapest approach on this list. The ask is a methods question: does an independent zebrafish sgRNA activity set exist that CRISPRscan has not seen, and if not, what is the smallest injection series that would produce one? A fair held-out comparison of CRISPRscan against the cross-species transfer our pipeline currently uses is a publishable negative result that costs him mostly judgement. WE would have to bring: the reimplementation and its verification (his 25 published scored sgRNAs reproduce at rho = 1.0000, max |difference| = 0.0000, at a coordinate offset we derived rather than assumed), the 307-guide table with GRCz11 coordinates, the seeded bootstrap, and the fact that the implementation failed its first run because reverse-complementing a genomic window flips its flanks.

openness_evidence.claim: Released CRISPRscan as a public scoring tool and published the full coefficient table, plus 25 scored sgRNAs that let a third party verify a reimplementation. We used exactly that.
Works in large cross-border consortia: the 2022 Nature Communications paper spans CABD, IDIBELL, CRG, Yale and Massachusetts General Hospital.
Treats "does my predictor transfer to a new setting" as a question worth publishing, which is the same question our benchmark asks.
openness_evidence.source: Our reading of doi 10.1038/s41467-022-30228-4 and doi 10.1038/s41467-017-01836-2. He has not invited this comparison.

candidates.caution: The headline we would be bringing him is that a model fitted on his assay beats two models that were not — which is a flattering result for him and an unflattering one for us, so there is little in it for him beyond the held-out test. A tool-development lab may also simply not care about a design pipeline it has no stake in. And 191 of his 499 guides did not match uniquely in GRCz11 under our exact-match rule; those 191 are a selection rather than a random sample, and he is quite likely to point out a locating method we got wrong before he points at anything else. Note also that a different researcher publishing as "M. A. Moreno-Mateos" works in computational mechanics; do not conflate the two records.

candidates.name: Kryn Stankunas
candidates.institution: University of Oregon, Department of Biology and Institute of Molecular Biology
candidates.field: Zebrafish fin regeneration and skeletal patterning; control of appendage outgrowth duration and organ size; ion and Hedgehog signalling in bone progenitors; mouse heart development.
candidates.why_relevant_to_delphi: His 2021 Development paper is the second of the three fin-size facts our bench brief is built on — the one that says homozygous loss of kcnh2a has no overt effect on fin length, so the informative edits are regulatory or gain-of-function. kcnh2a is also one of the two loci in our fin-ratio design. More importantly for us, his mechanism is TIME: fin size is set by how long outgrowth continues, not by a positional set-point. Our model has no time axis at all — every trait in the scorer is a single ratio measured once, which is exactly the structural reason only 1 of our 48 theorem-carrying laws is expressible on our trait set. If fin proportion is a rate-times-duration quantity, a one-shot ratio model is the wrong shape, and he is the person who can say so with data.

flagship_papers.title: longfin causes cis-ectopic expression of the kcnh2a ether-a-go-go K+ channel to autonomously prolong fin outgrowth
flagship_papers.why_it_matters: The source of the loss-of-function constraint that reshaped our bench plan, and of the duration-based model of fin size that our ratio-only trait set cannot express.

flagship_papers.title: Limited dedifferentiation provides replacement tissue during zebrafish fin regeneration
flagship_papers.why_it_matters: Lineage restriction means a fin is a set of per-ray units, not a single plastic field — a constraint our whole-fin ratio traits silently ignore.

flagship_papers.title: Shh promotes direct interactions between epidermal cells and osteoblast progenitors to shape regenerated zebrafish bone
flagship_papers.why_it_matters: Ray branching is a discrete, mechanistically dissected shape decision — a far better target for a testable computational prediction than a continuous ratio.

key_figures_or_findings: longfin-t2 overexpresses kcnh2a on chromosome 2; disrupting kcnh2a in cis rescues the phenotype, making longfin-t2 a regulatory kcnh2a allele (Development 2021, doi 10.1242/dev.199384, via PubMed).
Chemical inhibition of Kcnh2a during late-stage regeneration fully suppresses overgrowth, and calcineurin inhibition likewise acts late — so fin size is tuned by outgrowth DURATION (same paper).

Epidermal and intra-ray fibroblast and osteoblast lineages stay developmentally restricted through regeneration; no multipotent progenitor was found (Dev Biol 2012, doi 10.1016/j.ydbio.2012.02.031, via PubMed).
Shha from the epidermis, not osteoblast-derived Ihha, drives ray branching; Hh/Smo output is confined to a narrow distal regenerate zone (Development 2017, doi 10.1242/dev.143792, via PubMed).

real_quotes.quote: We conclude ion signaling within the growth-determining mesenchyme lineage controls fin size by tuning outgrowth periods rather than altering positional information or cell-level growth potency.
real_quotes.source_title: longfin causes cis-ectopic expression of the kcnh2a ether-a-go-go K+ channel to autonomously prolong fin outgrowth
real_quotes.context: Closing sentence of the published abstract (PubMed record for PMID 34061172). We cite it as the clearest published argument that our ratio-only, single-timepoint trait set is the wrong representation for fin size.

real_quotes.quote: We found no evidence for the existence of multipotent progenitors.
real_quotes.source_title: Limited dedifferentiation provides replacement tissue during zebrafish fin regeneration
real_quotes.context: From the published abstract (PubMed record for PMID 22426105). A negative result stated plainly, which is the register we want this outreach to be in.

public_record: Professor of Biology and Full Member of the Institute of Molecular Biology at the University of Oregon; the profile lists cell biology, developmental biology and genetics as research areas (https://imb.uoregon.edu/stankunas).

The profile describes three lab programmes: heart development, organ regeneration (zebrafish, with Scott Stewart), and chemical genetic technologies including TU-tagging developed with Chris Doe's lab.
Corresponding author on the 2017 and 2021 Development papers above.
candidates.collaboration_angle: The best-shaped ask on this list, because it is a modelling argument rather than a favour. If fin size is set by outgrowth duration, then the right computational object is a trajectory, not a ratio — and we already have a trajectory layer (development/) that returns fin length over age from published growth curves and labels every number measured, secondary, proxy or assumed. Proposal: he tells us what a duration-based prediction would have to look like to be falsifiable in his regeneration assay, and we build it; the bench arm only happens if the prediction survives that. WE would have to bring the trajectory layer with its provenance labels intact, an honest statement that the early-life portion of it is assumed rather than measured, and the law-expressibility result below, which is the formal version of his point.

openness_evidence.claim: Develops and publishes reusable methodology (TU-tagging for cell-type-specific nascent-RNA labelling) jointly with another lab at the same institution.
Characterised and published a uniquely effective Smo inhibitor (BMS-833923) as a community-usable tool alongside the biology.
Publishes clean negative results and model-discriminating experiments, which suggests a collaborator who would tell us our model is wrong early rather than late.
openness_evidence.source: Our reading of doi 10.1016/j.ydbio.2012.02.031 and doi 10.1242/dev.199384. Not a statement he has made.

candidates.caution: A smaller lab than several others here, split across heart and fin programmes, so bench capacity is genuinely scarce; the regeneration programme also runs on adult fish, which is the most expensive animal time there is. The deeper problem is on our side: his result implies our current trait representation is the wrong shape for the question, and we do not yet have a time-resolved scorer to replace it. Approaching him before we do would be asking him to design our model for us.

candidates.name: Kenneth D. Poss
candidates.institution: University of Wisconsin-Madison, Department of Cell and Regenerative Biology; Director of Regenerative Biology, Morgridge Institute for Research
candidates.field: Vertebrate regeneration in zebrafish: appendage (fin), heart and spinal cord; regeneration enhancer elements; injury-triggered gene regulation.
candidates.why_relevant_to_delphi: He built the one mechanism in this field that is explicitly engineerable: tissue regeneration enhancer elements, injury-activated regulatory sequences that can be wired to a chosen effector to change regenerative output. Our organism-design format exists to carry a design to a bench, and a TREE-driven cassette is the only published construct class we have found where "write a design, express it on injury, read a morphological outcome" is a described workflow rather than a hope. He is also the most useful possible critic of our bench packages: his lab routinely runs fin amputation with per-animal readouts, so he knows precisely what our power section is getting wrong.

flagship_papers.title: Modulation of tissue repair by regeneration enhancer elements
flagship_papers.why_it_matters: The engineerable control element our organism-design format would most want to emit, with tissue-specific modules already dissected.

flagship_papers.title: Voltage-gated sodium channel is required for innervation and regeneration of amputated adult zebrafish fins
flagship_papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
flagship_papers.why_it_matters: A third bioelectric component in fin outgrowth, from a temperature-sensitive forward screen — more evidence that our single-gene fin cases are under-specified.

flagship_papers.title: Keeping at arm's length during regeneration
flagship_papers.why_it_matters: States the positional-identity and completion problem — how a regenerate knows when to stop — which is the same question our fin-ratio target implicitly answers.

key_figures_or_findings: leptin b (lepb) is highly induced in regenerating zebrafish hearts and fins; a short upstream/distal DNA element acquires open-chromatin marks during regeneration and drives injury-dependent expression from minimal promoters (Nature 2016, doi 10.1038/nature17644, via PubMed).

That element is divisible into tissue-specific modules sufficient for expression in regenerating fins or hearts separately, and enhancer-effector transgenes using it controlled regeneration efficacy (same paper).

A temperature-sensitive mutation in the major neuronal voltage-gated sodium channel gene disrupts blastema formation and axon regrowth, but not morphogenesis of established regenerates (PNAS 2022, doi 10.1073/pnas.2200342119, via PubMed).

real_quotes.quote: Our findings provide evidence for 'tissue regeneration enhancer elements' (TREEs) that trigger gene expression in injury sites and can be engineered to modulate the regenerative potential of vertebrate organs.
real_quotes.source_title: Modulation of tissue repair by regeneration enhancer elements
real_quotes.context: Closing sentence of the published abstract (PubMed record for PMID 27049946). The word "engineered" is his, and it is why this is the one mechanism our design format could target without overclaiming.

real_quotes.quote: Although the limb or fin may be years removed from its initial creation by an embryonic primordium, the blastema that emerges at the injury site fashions a close mimic of adult form.
real_quotes.source_title: Keeping at arm's length during regeneration
real_quotes.context: From the published abstract of the review (PubMed record for PMID 24780734). It frames the completion problem our fin-ratio prediction would have to engage with.

public_record: Professor in the Department of Cell and Regenerative Biology, University of Wisconsin-Madison, and Director of Regenerative Biology at the Morgridge Institute for Research; the departmental page credits him with discovering heart regeneration in zebrafish and with identifying tissue regeneration enhancer elements (https://crb.wisc.edu/staff/poss-kenneth/).
The same page records that he was James B. Duke Professor of Regenerative Biology at Duke University from 2003 to 2024 — relevant because older lab links point at Duke.
Affiliated with the Howard Hughes Medical Institute during the Duke period, per the author affiliation on the 2014 Developmental Cell paper (doi 10.1016/j.devcel.2014.04.007, via PubMed).
candidates.collaboration_angle: The right ask is a design-format one, not an animal one: what would a TREE-based cassette have to specify, field by field, for his lab to consider it a complete and checkable design rather than a sketch? That is a direct test of whether our .organism format earns its claim to be portable. A bench arm, if it ever happened, would be a fin-amputation regeneration readout, which his lab runs as routine. WE would have to bring the format with its enforcement intact — every value carrying a kind and a scope, the reader refusing a file rather than guessing one — plus the honest headline that on our own example design a simulator may use 2 of 15 values, 9 are not-established, and the axis the whole design claim rests on is not one the pre-registered scorecard could score.

openness_evidence.claim: Published TREEs as an engineerable, transferable element class and showed the element activating in injured neonatal mouse tissue — i.e. framed for reuse outside the original system.
Multi-institution collaboration is normal practice: the 2022 PNAS paper is a joint Wisconsin, Duke and Academia Sinica effort in which his lab contributed to work led elsewhere.
A newly built institute programme is usually the moment a lab is most open to new methodological partners — but this is our guess about timing, not anything he has said.

candidates.caution: The weakest fit of the fin-side candidates on subject matter: his question is regeneration, ours is morphological proportion, and the overlap is the tissue rather than the problem. He also runs one of the most visible regeneration programmes in the world and has just moved institutions, which is the single worst time to ask for bench capacity. And we have nothing he needs: no reagent, no dataset he lacks, and a scoring layer whose two external benchmarks came out at chance. If the format critique is not interesting to him on its own merits, there is no second reason for him to reply.

candidates.name: Michel Bagnat
candidates.institution: Duke University, Department of Cell Biology
candidates.field: Morphogenesis of the vertebrate axial skeleton in zebrafish; notochord vacuole biology; tissue mechanics and physical self-organisation of the spine.
candidates.why_relevant_to_delphi: He does the thing our morphology scorer most conspicuously cannot: derive a body proportion from a physical mechanism instead of from a distribution of observed specimens. Our worst failure is precisely of that kind — a law-derived constraint says the dorsal fin lies on the body (predorsal <= 1 SL), and the scorer rates an animal whose dorsal fin begins 1.02 standard lengths from the snout, past the end of the fish, as more typical than 4,068 of 4,673 real specimens (87.1%), at q = 0.347 against a median real fish of 0.650. candidates.name: Sijbren Otto
candidates.institution: Centre for Systems Chemistry, Stratingh Institute for Chemistry, University of Groningen, Groningen, the Netherlands
candidates.field: origins-of-life-protocells
candidates.why_relevant_to_delphi: He has a running system in which replication, selection, diversification and the beginnings of metabolism all emerge from molecules nobody designed for the purpose - and, critically, he reports the DIRECTION the system drifts without intervention: toward lower complexity, because smaller replicators replicate faster. That is a constraint on open-ended design that no genome-level model contains, and it is the kind of statement our registry should be able to hold.

flagship_papers.title: Mechanosensitive Self-Replication Driven by Self-Organization
flagship_papers.why_it_matters: The founding result: self-assembly in a mixture of interconverting oligomers produces self-replication, with mechanical agitation driving exponential growth. Replication as a consequence of physical organisation, not of encoded instructions.

flagship_papers.title: An Approach to the De Novo Synthesis of Life
flagship_papers.why_it_matters: The programme statement, and unusually explicit about what remains undone: compartmentalisation and open-ended evolution. A model for how to write a roadmap that names its own holes.

key_figures_or_findings: The replicator systems show spontaneous diversification onto different food sets, history dependence of replicator composition, and the spontaneous emergence of parasitic behaviour - three population-level phenomena arising with no genome at all.

Peptide-based replicator assemblies were found to organise their peptide units so as to create microenvironments capable of catalysis, including of the reactions producing their own precursors - reported as the first examples of assimilating a proto-metabolism.

Operating the replicators in a chemically fuelled out-of-equilibrium replication-destruction regime promoted increases in molecular complexity, counteracting an inherent drift toward lower complexity. The drift direction is the transferable finding.

what_we_would_be_asking.summary: A powerable version of our top-ranked zebrafish experiment is about 30 scorable animals per arm and roughly $169 in marginal consumables. That is small. It is also not the cost: the real cost is skilled time, not consumables. What we would actually be asking for is a trained person, a microinjection rig and four months of tank space, and we should say so first rather than lead with the cheap number.

the_small_number.what_that_number_counts: Scorable adults that carry fin-expressing clones — NOT injected embryos. Two unpublished fractions sit between this number and the embryos to inject: survival of injected embryos to adulthood in that facility on that mix, and the fraction of surviving adults with marker-positive cells in the fins. The published effect size is conditioned on the second fraction, and the conditioning fraction itself is not published.
the_small_number.arms_detail: Two published controls (marker-only, and a non-conductive channel variant) plus two doses. The controls are the experiment here, not an accessory to it.
the_small_number.marginal_consumables_basis: What the package adds in a lab that already runs zebrafish injections. The whole parts list is $3,136.52, of which $2,967.92 is bulk salts, consumables and general kits such a lab already owns. Every price is a public list price read from the vendor page on a recorded date. No price is a quote; none includes shipping, tax or surcharges; academic buyers pay less on contract.
the_small_number.the_number_is_a_lower_bound: The construct is not in Addgene or any searchable repository. In the source paper it was built from two gift plasmids and the specificity variant was made by PCR mutagenesis, so this line is either a request to a corresponding author — free, but on their timetable and subject to an MTA — or a cloning project of three constructs.
the_small_number.statistics_caveat: The smallest expected cell count in the binding comparison is 0.200, below the usual 5 at which the normal approximation is trusted. Use Fisher’s exact test and expect it to need slightly MORE animals than 30, not fewer.

the_real_cost: A skilled person’s weeks. Microinjection of one-cell zygotes, raising injected fish to adulthood, blind scoring of a morphological endpoint, and per-animal record keeping. Labour is the largest real cost of all and is not in the $169 or the $3,136.
About four months to an answer, because the readout is in adults. Four months of tank space is a scheduling commitment, not a consumable.
Husbandry and facility costs, which for any case needing a generation dominate everything in the parts list.

Imaging and scoring time: fluorescence screening of larvae, then adult scoring of local overgrowth against marker-positive mesenchyme in the same fin. Blind scoring costs more time than unblinded scoring, and we are asking for blind scoring.
Capital we cannot supply: microinjection rig, stereoscope, micromanipulator, incubator. A lab either has these or the request is not addressed to the right lab.

Institutional animal-care approval (IACUC or local equivalent) and biosafety registration for the nuclease and any synthetic nucleic acid, covering this line, these numbers and these endpoints. We cannot grant any of it and nothing starts without it.
Institutional overhead, shipping, tax and vendor surcharges — one supplier in our list never publishes shipping at all.

A missing positive control. There is no recorded published candidate for a construct known to integrate and express in fin tissue in a given facility. A lab new to this transgenesis route should run one before committing four months of tank space, and that pilot is on them, not us.
The opportunity cost of saying yes: the same person, the same rig and the same tanks are the binding constraint on the lab’s own programme.
what_a_fair_ask_looks_like: Ask for criticism before asking for animals. The first request is "tell us what is wrong with this before anyone orders anything" — blunt is more useful than polite — and it comes with the traps list, the stop rules and the ordering files.
If our own power section refuses for lack of a number, that missing number is a literature or source-data question, not bench time. Do not spend a partner’s animals on our homework.

Prefer asks with no animals in them at all where one exists: a trait-representation audit, a gene-identity audit, a constraint-derivation conversation, a physical model, or reuse of an already-open 3D corpus.
Offer a scope the lab can decline in one line without it being awkward, and accept the decline.
If it is run: blind scoring, both controls in the same session from the same clutch, per-animal values rather than summaries, and the return format supplied in advance.

what_we_bring_honestly.stance: Two of the three levels of our system come out at chance against external ground truth and one passes. A partner should hear all three before deciding, and should hear them from us rather than discover them.

negative_results.claim: The score we rank CRISPR guides by is statistically indistinguishable from no information on zebrafish.
negative_results.numbers: Against 307 sgRNAs with activity measured in injected zebrafish embryos: Doench 2014 Rule Set 1, which our edit planner actually uses, gives Spearman rho = -0.037, 95% CI [-0.149, 0.073]. Our own heuristic gives 0.082, CI [-0.024, 0.196]. Both intervals straddle zero and Doench’s point estimate is slightly negative. CRISPRscan, fitted on zebrafish injections, reaches 0.269, CI [0.165, 0.364] — and that is an upper bound rather than an estimate, because it is being scored on the study that fitted it.
negative_results.what_it_means_for_a_partner: If we hand you a ranked guide list, the ranking carries no demonstrated information for your organism. We cannot promise you a good guide. This is a fact about OUR ranking, not a criticism of Doench 2014, which never claimed to transfer and whose own module text in our codebase calls it a transfer across species and assay.

negative_results.claim: Our morphology scorer is a plausibility model, not a viability model, and distance to real fish does not bound anatomical possibility.
negative_results.numbers: Decoy-difficulty curve: AUC 0.891 against shuffled negatives falls to 0.536 — chance — against real fish nudged a quarter of a standard deviation. 12,152 of our 12,606 held-out negatives were shuffles, and a shuffle destroys exactly and only the trait-trait correlation a Mahalanobis distance detects. A constructed animal whose snout and eye overhang the back of its head by 2% of body length — no room for braincase, jaw, gills or operculum — scores q = 0.918 and ranks more plausible than 1,279 of 4,673 real fish; 20,000 draws from the fitted model never found it and a search found it at once. The worst law-derived violator is worse: a dorsal fin beginning 1.02 standard lengths from the snout, past the end of the fish, at q = 0.347, more typical than 4,068 of 4,673 real specimens (87.1%), against a median real fish of 0.650.
negative_results.what_it_means_for_a_partner: If we tell you a designed animal is plausible, we have told you it is close to the specimen cloud, and nothing about whether it could exist. The failure is specific to constraints whose boundary lies just outside the observed marginal range — which is where most anatomical impossibilities live.

negative_results.claim: Only 1 of the 48 theorem-carrying laws in our formal registry is expressible as a constraint on our own trait set — a rate of 2.1%.
negative_results.numbers: The ten traits are all length divided by standard length for one specimen; the registry mostly speaks in quantities those traits do not carry — two sizes (every allometry), a population, a power or oxygen budget, a genotype. One law is worse than unmeasurable: dividing an area by SL squared IS the law, so on normalised traits it is a tautology with nothing to forbid. The near miss is the instructive one: a law bounds pectoral fin LENGTH / SL to [0.406, 0.823] while our trait block carries the snout-to-fin-BASE distance — two words apart, unrelated measurements — and treating them as the same quantity would have applied a bound from 49 museum specimens to a different number entirely.
negative_results.what_it_means_for_a_partner: A law we cannot evaluate on our data is not yet a constraint on our design. When we say a design satisfies our formal layer, for 47 of 48 laws that statement is vacuous on the traits we actually carry.

what_does_pass.claim: The formal layer itself holds up, and it is the one thing we can offer without qualification.
what_does_pass.numbers: All 48 laws carrying a Lean module and theorem also carry a machine-checked non-vacuity witness, depending only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound — no sorry, no project-specific axiom. In mutation testing, 1 mutant was refuted and the control behaved. A theorem with unsatisfiable hypotheses is vacuously true and proves nothing; this is the first thing to check in a law registry and the check most registries have no field for.
what_does_pass.honest_scope: Two targets and three mutants. A method and a first result, not a coverage figure over the 48 laws.

also_true_and_also_unflattering: On our own flagship design, the portable organism file declares 15 values of which 9 are not-established and 4 assumed; a simulator may use 2 of them. The pre-registered scorecard could score 1 of 10 declared phenotypic axes, and the axis the whole design claim rests on — pectoral fin length / SL — is not the one it could score.

Our development layer does not simulate development. Length grows along a published curve and proportions change along fits to measured specimens; nothing models cells, genes or tissues producing a shape. Several relations in it are labelled assumed or assumed transfer, including the fin-area law, and the wing loading it implies disagrees with the published exponent.

Our CRISPRscan reimplementation failed on its first run, because the genomic windows were built from scan coordinates that are correct on the plus strand and wrong on the minus strand. Only 5 of 25 protospacers sat where the arithmetic said, and the offset sweep then showed a best fit at the WRONG offset. We keep that in the record on purpose.
We have no animals, no facility, no approvals and no reagents. Everything we can contribute is code, derivations, provenance discipline and benchmarks that are allowed to come out badly.
what_we_bring_honestly.why_this_is_stated_up_front: A productivity figure cannot come out badly. "61 laws registered" and "AUC 0.89" measure how much was built. A benchmark has to be able to come out badly, which means the answer has to come from somewhere the system does not control. Ours did, twice, and came out at chance. A careful scientist should weigh that before giving us a person’s weeks, and would be right to say no.

xenobots-synthetic-living-machines.why: This cluster IS goal one. "Agentic biomaterials" has no other referent in the current literature: organisms assembled from cells whose agency does the construction, with no genome edit anywhere in the pipeline. It sits in the generation layer because what it supplies is a design surface - and it is the layer where we are most exposed, because our generator cannot address that surface at all. It also serves goal two, since the field's own stated purpose includes finding what shapes cells can be induced to adopt, which is a constraint discovery programme.
xenobots-synthetic-living-machines.what_it_would_change_here: It would force the organism format to acquire a representation of cell ARRANGEMENT as an input, not just as stored geometry, and would force the generator to have an operator that proposes one.

comparative-genomics-ortholog-conjecture.why: The ortholog conjecture is a biological "law" that our analogy module uses as a premise in an inference: this gene is the orthologue, therefore it does that job here too. The literature does not come out cleanly - one careful study finds the conjecture holds weakly after bias correction, another finds strong evidence against it in the prediction setting - so the premise is not safe. That makes this an inference-layer problem: the question is not what the world is but what follows from what, and the answer is less than we assumed.
comparative-genomics-ortholog-conjecture.what_it_would_change_here: It would turn the orthologue step from an unstated premise into a stated one with a measured reliability, and it would force the four annotation confounders into our code.

biomechanics-functional-morphology.why: These are the people who can say NO on evidence about a body plan. They measure what a shape can actually do, in units, with error bars. That is the disclosure layer's entire job: not to propose and not to derive, but to measure against the world and refuse. Our repository already contains the failure this cluster exists to catch - a design scorer calling a geometrically impossible animal typical - and only a measurement could catch it.
biomechanics-functional-morphology.what_it_would_change_here: It would attach a measurement procedure to every geometric or performance constraint we assert, so that a constraint which cannot be tested is visibly marked as untested rather than scored.

theoretical-mathematical-biology.why: Goal two is reverse-engineering biological laws, and this cluster is the only one with a track record of auditing what a biological law's derivation actually licenses - finite-size corrections to a scaling exponent, accessibility metrics on phenotype space, rule-based formalisms with static analysis behind them. It is squarely the inference layer, and it is where our characteristic failure lives: a theorem can be sound, compile, and say nothing, or say something other than its English gloss.
theoretical-mathematical-biology.what_it_would_change_here: It would require every law in the registry to carry its approximation regime and assumption set, and would supply an external standard for whether a formalisation is non-vacuous.

origins-of-life-protocells.why: Goal three names origins of life explicitly. It belongs to the disclosure layer for the reason this repository has already recorded: it is the limiting case of aletheia as un-forgetting. The event left almost no record, and the record it left has been overwritten by its own descendants, so the honest output is mostly a careful account of what is not known. It also touches goal one, because a protocell is a living system built without a genome to edit - the same category of object as a biobot, reached from chemistry.
origins-of-life-protocells.what_it_would_change_here: Almost nothing, today, and that is the point: it is the cluster where the correct contribution is to listen and to mark what we cannot represent. See THE_HONEST_GAP.

xenobots-synthetic-living-machines.what_a_partner_would_want: A system that proposes a construct: these cell types, in this arrangement, at this scale, predicted to do this - and a buildability filter that rules out the arrangements their wet lab cannot realise.
xenobots-synthetic-living-machines.what_we_have: An organism format that can STORE a genome and per-cell geometry, a simulation engine, a design scorer, a law registry, a Lean layer, and a holdout.
xenobots-synthetic-living-machines.what_we_cannot_offer_today: The design surface itself. Our generator's output is an EDIT LIST AGAINST A REFERENCE ASSEMBLY. Every proposal it can make has the form "change this base, this gene, this allele in an existing organism". NOTHING IN THE PIPELINE CAN PROPOSE A CELL ARRANGEMENT. The formats represent genomes and they represent per-cell geometry, but geometry is only ever read back from something that already exists; there is no operator anywhere that takes a desired behaviour and emits a spatial configuration of cells. Since a cell arrangement is THE ENTIRE DESIGN SURFACE for this field, we cannot express a single candidate design in it. Not badly - at all.
xenobots-synthetic-living-machines.the_blunt_version: We cannot say "take these cells and put them there". That sentence is the field, and our vocabulary has no way to write it down. On this cluster we are not a weaker design partner, we are not a design partner.
xenobots-synthetic-living-machines.what_we_could_honestly_offer_instead: The constraint and audit side: formalising a buildability filter, recording provenance, stating a morphology-to-behaviour claim precisely enough to be falsified by their next build. Useful, secondary, and not what they would ask for first.
xenobots-synthetic-living-machines.what_would_have_to_change: A representation whose primitive is a positioned cell population rather than a sequence variant, and a generator with a proposal operator over that representation. That is new work, not a configuration change.

comparative-genomics-ortholog-conjecture.what_a_partner_would_want: A method submitted to a shared benchmark, with controls for the known annotation biases, and a clear separation between claims about how function evolves and claims about how to predict it.
comparative-genomics-ortholog-conjecture.what_we_have: An analogy module that maps a requested trait onto an orthologue and scores the mapping.
comparative-genomics-ortholog-conjecture.what_we_cannot_offer_today: A benchmarked orthology method, or any external validation of our orthologue calls. We control for none of the four confounders the 2012 paper enumerates, we do not distinguish graph-based from tree-based orthology, and we have never submitted anything to the community benchmark. We also have no functional data of our own - every number we would bring is derived from their resources.
comparative-genomics-ortholog-conjecture.the_blunt_version: We are a consumer of this field's output that has never been measured by this field's yardstick, and we are using as a premise a conjecture that two careful groups cannot agree on.
comparative-genomics-ortholog-conjecture.what_we_could_honestly_offer_instead: Ourselves as a test case: run our module against the benchmark, publish the failures, and contribute the negative result. That is a real contribution and it costs them almost nothing.
comparative-genomics-ortholog-conjecture.what_would_have_to_change: Implement the bias controls, split the evolution question from the prediction question in our own code, and stop ranking orthologues first until we can show it helps.

biomechanics-functional-morphology.what_a_partner_would_want: Predictions with units, error bars, and a mechanism - something a high-speed camera or a force plate could contradict.
biomechanics-functional-morphology.what_we_have: A design scorer, a physics layer, and a glide/envelope analysis that returned inconclusive on most of what it was asked.
biomechanics-functional-morphology.what_we_cannot_offer_today: A performance prediction anyone could falsify. Our scores are relative plausibility, not forces, velocities or powers. Most of our envelope results are inconclusive, and our one documented scorer failure was a body plan that is geometrically impossible being ranked as typical - which means the scorer was not measuring mechanics at all. We have no experimental capability whatsoever: no specimens, no rig, no measurements of our own.
biomechanics-functional-morphology.the_blunt_version: We would be asking them to measure our guesses. That is a legitimate thing to ask for, but it is a favour, not a collaboration, until we can state a constraint with units and a procedure.
biomechanics-functional-morphology.what_we_could_honestly_offer_instead: Formalisation of their own principles into checkable constraints with explicit measurement procedures, plus a systematic search of our inventory for specimens that violate them.
biomechanics-functional-morphology.what_would_have_to_change: Dimensional quantities throughout the scorer, an uncertainty model, and a rule that an untestable constraint is marked not-established rather than scored.

theoretical-mathematical-biology.what_a_partner_would_want: Formal statements that are non-vacuous, whose informal glosses match their formal content, and whose domains of validity are explicit.
theoretical-mathematical-biology.what_we_have: A 62-law registry, a Lean layer with proved theorems, and mutation benchmarks over them.
theoretical-mathematical-biology.what_we_cannot_offer_today: An assurance that our formal statements say what we claim. Our registry stores laws WITHOUT their approximation regimes, which is exactly the failure the finite-size scaling audit documents. Our own recorded failure mode is a theorem that is sound and says nothing, and its quieter cousin - a theorem whose English gloss does not match its formal statement - passes every check we currently have. Several of our flagship results are marked inconclusive.
theoretical-mathematical-biology.the_blunt_version: A formal-methods partner would read our registry and find the vacuity before we finished describing it. We should lead with that rather than be caught by it.
theoretical-mathematical-biology.what_we_could_honestly_offer_instead: A domain they have not formalised - whole-organism form and constraint - and a corpus of candidate laws, offered as material to be stress-tested rather than as results.
theoretical-mathematical-biology.what_would_have_to_change: Approximation regimes and assumption sets as required fields on every registry law, and a gloss-versus-formal-content check that can actually fail.

origins-of-life-protocells.what_a_partner_would_want: Chemistry, or a formalism that already handles non-genomic replicators and out-of-equilibrium systems, or data.
origins-of-life-protocells.what_we_cannot_offer_today: We have nothing to offer this field yet, and that is the whole of the honest answer. No chemistry, no protocell capability, no out-of-equilibrium modelling, and no representation that can describe a replicator with no genome - our organism format's primitives are a reference assembly and its variants, which presupposes exactly the thing origins research is trying to explain the arrival of. Goal three names this field and we come to it empty-handed.
origins-of-life-protocells.the_blunt_version: We should not approach this cluster as a collaborator. We should approach it as a student, through the open community that already exists, and we should say in the first sentence that we have nothing to offer yet.
origins-of-life-protocells.what_we_could_honestly_offer_instead: At most, bookkeeping: a formal record of mutually antagonistic constraints a built system must satisfy at once, with provenance, so a requirement satisfied in one subsystem is not silently violated by another. Offered, not proposed.
origins-of-life-protocells.what_would_have_to_change: A representation whose primitive is a population of interconverting molecules rather than a genome. That is a different project, not an extension of this one.

the_honest_gap.the_sharpest_one: Xenobots. Our formats represent genomes and they represent per-cell geometry, but NOTHING IN THE PIPELINE CAN PROPOSE A CELL ARRANGEMENT - and a cell arrangement is the entire design surface for that field. Our generator emits edit lists against a reference assembly, so every design it can express presupposes an organism that already has the body we would be trying to specify. The field our first stated goal points at is the one field whose design problem we cannot write down.
the_honest_gap.the_rule: Each gap above is stated in the terms a partner in that field would use, and names the specific missing capability rather than a general shortfall. A gap described vaguely enough to sound modest is a gap being hidden.
